overview:
Greg Stanton seeks another term in this Phoenix-area district, which leans Democratic by about four points. He enters the general election with a commanding financial edge: roughly $1.9 million on hand after raising $2.7 million, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has about $90,000 available. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent, and prediction markets give him roughly a 96% chance of victory.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. The district's Democratic tilt, incumbency, and a favorable national environment point to a comfortable Stanton win, with the money gap reinforcing that picture. Jasser, a known but heavily outspent challenger, faces steep odds. A late surge of outside spending or a sudden turn in the national mood would be the most plausible forces to make this competitive.
